column1: # The team modes: the skills and plugins the rules name, which every agent tool on the machine
# has installed, one definition for every tool.
# Columns: tool <TAB> mode <TAB> probe <TAB> install <TAB> verified
# No work starts until every row of the tool a session runs in is installed. This file is what
# holds that: session-start and start-issue run team-modes-check, which reads the rows for the
# tools found on this machine and refuses the session when a mode is missing, printing the
# install column for it. team-modes-install runs that column. The push hook runs the same check,
# so a push cannot go out of a session that never had them.
# tool     the agent tool, by the name of its command on PATH: claude, codex, gemini, agy. A tool
#          whose command has another name gets its own rows once somebody who uses it adds them.
# mode     archify (interactive diagrams, the skill rules/skills.md names for documenting a
#          structure). The tool loads it when a task calls for it.
# probe    how the check sees that the mode is installed for that tool:
#            plugin:NAME  the tool's own plugin list names it (claude plugin list,
#                         codex plugin list, gemini extensions list, agy plugin list)
#            skill:NAME   a skill folder of that name exists in the tool's skill directories
#                         or in the shared .agents/skills directory the skills installer writes
#            file:PATH    that file exists (~ is the home directory)
#            none         nobody has written a probe yet - the check REFUSES and says so, so the
#                         first person who uses the tool fills the row in rather than guessing
#            always       counts as installed; only for tests
# install  the command that installs it, run by team-modes-install; "-" where the tool's own
#          documentation is the only source (the check prints its address instead)
#          Every command installs a fixed version: a skill a tag or commit through the tree URL of
#          the skills CLI, a Claude marketplace a tag (#<tag>; it takes no commit), a Codex
#          marketplace and a Gemini extension a --ref. A newer version comes in by changing the
#          row and verifying it again.
#          agy does not read the shared ~/.agents/skills folder (measured on agy 1.4.0), and
#          archify ships no plugin for it, so its row wraps the installed skill in a plugin folder
#          and hands that to agy plugin install.
# verified LOGIN,DATE of the person who ran the probe and the install on that tool, or "-".
#          A row marked "-" is a reading of the mode's documentation, not a proof.
claude
codex
gemini
agy
column4: npx -y skills@1.7.0 add https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/5289f6867f048a7450ec5718f58459613a84cf41/archify -g -a antigravity-cli -y && d="$(mktemp -d)" && { mkdir "$d/skills" && cp -R ~/.agents/skills/archify "$d/skills/" && printf '{"name":"archify"}\n' > "$d/plugin.json" && agy plugin install "$d"; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit "$s"; }
